comment: ST-01's register: every standard a part of the Prism answers to, the parts it governs (path globs over PT-01's parts, test/parts/parts.txt), and its own normative text pinned by SHA-256 ('text', or 'oracle' to reuse an oracle source's pin). Each inventory names an extractor, tools/standards/extract/<extract>.py, that turns the pinned bytes into requirements (test/standards/requirements.json). A requirement is enforced when a suite that reaches a governed part carries 'enforces: <id>', or 'enforcedBy' names that suite for it; every other requirement is debt (debt.json), which only shrinks. A standard without a pinned text says why: 'withheld' (its issuer does not publish it) or 'unpinned' (what it waits on). A part no standard governs is listed under 'ungoverned' with the reason none applies, or under 'unassigned', which only shrinks. Run python3 -I tools/standards/gate.py --check.

ungoverned.app/src/PrismDestRoute.lex.tex: a reader of the Prism's own in front of its destinations decision: it states that decision's request from the facts of one item (app/specs/dest/spec.json names the fields), and no external standard specifies it
ungoverned.app/src/PrismAsk.lex.tex: a decision of the Prism's own (what it does with words said to it), specified by no external standard: its requirements are its spec's rules and properties (app/specs/ask/spec.json), proved in LexLean
